top_signal.title: How do small businesses decide which numbers to trust when revenue is growing but cash keeps getting tighter?
top_signal.summary: A business can report stronger sales every month and still find itself struggling to cover payroll, supplier payments, or tax obligations. Sometimes the issue is slow collections; other times, inventory, customer payment terms, or growth expenses are absorbing cash faster than expected.   What makes this difficult is that the business may look healthy on paper, and cutting costs or pushing for more sales doesn't necessarily solve the underlying problem.   For owners who have experienced this, what was the metric or early warning sign that helped you identify the real issue before it became a serious cash-flow problem? Was it cash conversion, receivables ageing, contribution margin, or something less obvious?       submitted by     /u/SmartTechInsights       [link]       [comments]
